Maintenance Report — MNT-0180-007

Asset: WELL-0180 (NE-08 Well 180, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 25 Feb 2024 08:00 · Finished: 05 Mar 2024 14:00 · Well stopped for this job: 222 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0180-0069 on 2024-02-22 Report written: 06 Mar 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0180-0069 showed the wellhead at 13.2 °C with the air at 12.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 7 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0180-007 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0180-013

Asset: WELL-0180 (NE-08 Well 180, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 12 Oct 2024 08:00 · Finished: 23 Oct 2024 14:00 · Well stopped for this job: 270 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0180-0102 on 2024-10-10 Report written: 24 Oct 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0180-0102 showed the wellhead at 26.8 °C with the air at 21.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
  • Start a root-cause analysis for this equipment before the next repair is closed (well-type manual, section 10).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0180-016

Asset: WELL-0180 (NE-08 Well 180, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: rod string Work started: 12 Jan 2025 08:00 · Finished: 21 Jan 2025 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 220 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0180-0115 on 2025-01-09 Report written: 22 Jan 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0180-0115 showed the wellhead at 13.7 °C with the air at 12.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 7 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Labour (company crew and contractor)5,255

Notes and recommendations

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor treatment for this well.
  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil

Maintenance Report — MNT-0180-025

Asset: WELL-0180 (NE-08 Well 180, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 10 Apr 2026 08:00 · Finished: 11 Apr 2026 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 20 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0180-0180 on 2026-04-09 Report written: 13 Apr 2026

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0180-0180 at 09:00 on 2026-04-09 found crude oil on the pad: about 1.2% of the pad area, estimated 0.7 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 6.4 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 249 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 199 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.5 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0180-025 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.31% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Absorbents and berms535
Soil hauling and disposal936
Labour (company crew)2,832
Total5,506
